ai.description: *Walkerana phrynoderma* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown, warty dorsum and cream-colored belly. It features a distinct dark lateral band and prominent, elongated toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Walkerana phrynoderma* is best distinguished by the prominent, coarse, and irregular glandular warts covering its dorsal skin, which are absent in other *Walkerana* species.
ai.habitat: *Walkerana phrynoderma* inhabits high-altitude evergreen montane forests (sholas) in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Walkerana phrynoderma* is primarily nocturnal, often found perched on wet rocks near cascading streams where it actively hunts for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Walkerana phrynoderma* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of eggs in moist rocky crevices near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Walkerana phrynoderma* is endemic to the high-elevation montane rainforests of the southern Western Ghats, specifically restricted to the Munnar region in Kerala, India.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Walkerana phrynoderma* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from within rocky, high-altitude stream habitats.
